reason: I'll start by fitting the bearing frames to the base, giving the rotating mechanism support.
expectation: I expect a base ready to hold the crankshaft, though I don't know the exact fitting order.

alternatives.reason: The rod and guide also look useful, but I prefer to build the base first.

effect: The bearing frames are in place, so the base is ready for the shaft.
reason: I'll fit the crankshaft into its bearings to build the rotating part.
expectation: The shaft should sit in the bearings and be able to turn.

alternatives.reason: The follower assembly is also needed, but I'd like to finish the shaft first.

effect: The crankshaft turns in the frame, ready for the cam.
reason: I'll add the off-centre cam to the turning shaft so it can eventually lift the follower.
expectation: I expect the cam to rotate with the shaft, though the follower will still need fitting.

alternatives.reason: The follower and guide are also needed, but I'd like to complete the rotating assembly first.

effect: The cam's off-centre shape makes its edge rise and fall as the shaft turns, explaining how it can move the follower.
reaction: The comparison with a centred disc makes the mechanism clear.
reason: I'll assemble the follower and guide; it's the only offered combination and should prepare the moving rod.
expectation: I expect the guide to keep the follower rod moving in a straight line, ready to meet the cam.

effect: The follower is assembled in its guide and can now be joined to the cam mechanism.
reason: I'll join the follower to the cam assembly; it's the only offered combination and should connect the rotating and sliding parts.
expectation: I expect the cam to lift the guided rod as it turns, though the spring and handle may still need fitting.

effect: The guided follower is now positioned above the cam, connecting the rotating and sliding parts.
reaction: The mechanism is coming together straightforwardly.
reason: I'll add the crank handle; it's the only offered combination and should let me turn the shaft.
expectation: I expect the handle to turn the cam and move the follower, though the spring may still need fitting.

effect: The test reveals that the rod can stick and lose contact with the descending cam, so it needs help returning.
reaction: The imperfect first test makes the spring's purpose clearer.
reason: I'll add the spring; it's the only offered combination and should help keep the follower against the cam.
expectation: I expect the spring to press the follower back toward the cam so the rod rises and falls reliably.

effect: The spring keeps the follower against the cam, completing a reliable conversion from rotation to up-and-down motion.
reaction: Satisfying to see the failed test resolved and the mechanism working.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the handle was most worthwhile: the follower lost contact, giving the spring a clear practical purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: The early bearing and shaft fittings were straightforward but less engaging individually.

surprise.text: I didn't expect the light rod to hang in its guide rather than follow the cam down.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the offered fittings had understandable roles, though several were the only available combination.

continue.text: Yes. The cam explanation and the troubleshooting were worth the time, and I'd be curious to see how the mechanism makes the dragon wave.
